claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Now, to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after Alex day-to-day - I make sure he's fed, clothed, and all his needs are taken care of.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation arranged by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex is fostered - I'm fostering him. The local authority gives me maintenance for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex is fostered and that the local authority is providing maintenance for him. This is an important detail.

To be completely clear for the assessment:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation as well as the maintenance, or is it just maintenance payments?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the council pays for both his accommodation and maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old and lives with you
- You live in the UK and are responsible for his day-to-day care
- Alex is fostered
- The local council is paying towards both his accommodation and maintenance

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can get Child Benefit if you foster a child, **as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance**. 

Unfortunately, since the local council is paying towards both Alex's accommodation and maintenance, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you would be **ineligible** for Child Benefit for Alex in this situation. The determining factor is that the local council is providing payments towards his accommodation and maintenance as part of the fostering arrangement.

If your circumstances change in the future, you may want to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.
